Ōtorii (photographed August 26, 2019) {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=250|coord={{coord|35|28|14.8|N|138|47|32.6|E}}}} |location={{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市}} Kamiyoshida 5558 |latitude_deg=35|latitude_min=28|latitude_sec=14.8|N/S=N |longitude_deg=138|longitude_min=47|longitude_sec=32.6|E/W=E |map_country_code=JP |map=Japan Yamanashi |deity={{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}
{{ill|Ninigi|ja|天孫彦火瓊瓊杵命}}
{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}} |shintai= |shakaku=Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|近代Rank制度#諸社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|ja|富士山}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration."{{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fuji cult|ja|富士講}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|shukubō|ja|宿坊}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市}} Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線}} {{ill|Mt. Fuji Station|ja|富士山駅}}. ==Related Articles== * {{ill|Yoshida Fire festival|ja|吉田の火祭}} * {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|ja|富士講}} * {{ill|Gekkō-ji Temple|ja|月江寺}} * {{ill|Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|ja|冨士御室浅間神社}} * {{ill|Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|ja|冨士山下宮小室浅間神社}} * {{ill|Kōshū Dōguyū|ja|郡内大工仲間}} * {{ill|Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|ja|三國第一山新倉富士浅間神社}} ==References== {{Reflist}} 大鳥居（2019年8月26日撮影）

[[大山祇神]] |神体 = |社格 = 旧[[近代社格制度#諸社|県社]]
[[別表神社]] |創建 = （伝）[[景行天皇]]40年
（[[日本武尊]]東征時） |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = 初申祭 5月5日 |神事 = }} '''北口本宮冨士浅間神社'''（きたぐちほんぐうふじせんげんじんじゃ）は、[[山梨県]][[富士吉田市]]上吉田にある[[神社]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[近代社格制度#諸社|県社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 [[富士登山]]吉田口登山道の起点にあたり、「[[富士山-信仰の対象と芸術の源泉]]」の構成資産のひとつである「富士山域」の一部として[[世界文化遺産]]に登録されている。 == 祭神 == * [[木花開耶姫命]]（このはなさくやひめのみこと） * 天孫[[ニニギ|彦火瓊瓊杵命]]（てんそんひこほのににぎのみこと） - 夫神 * [[大山祇神]]（おおやまづみのかみ） - 父神 == 大祭 == * 新年祭 - [[2月17日]] * 初申祭（例祭） - [[5月5日]] * [[吉田の火祭|鎮火祭（吉田の火祭り）]] - [[8月26日]]、[[8月27日|27日]] * 新嘗祭 - [[11月23日]] == 由緒 == [[景行天皇]]40年に、[[日本武尊]]が東方遠征の折、箱根足柄より[[甲斐国]][[酒折宮]]に向かう途次、当地を通過、「富士の神山は北方より登拝せよと」、祠を建てて祀ったのが始まりとされている。 [[延暦]]7年（788年）に甲斐守である[[紀豊庭]]により現在地に神殿を建て、浅間の大神を祀り、大塚丘には日本武尊の神霊を祀った。以後、逐次造営、改築され、現在の本殿は[[元和 (日本)|元和]]元年（[[1615年]]）、谷村城主の鳥居土佐守成次の寄進により建立された。その後、[[貞享]]5年（1688年）に社殿が造修された。 [[享保]]18年（1733年）、江戸の[[富士講]]村上派を率いる[[村上光清]]が私財を投じて出資し、幣殿、拝殿、神楽殿、手水舎、隋神門を造営させた。 これは、[[郡内大工仲間]]による最大規模の造営となり、中でも拝殿は最大の建築物である。 拝殿の前の両脇には樹齢千年の「富士太郎杉」「富士夫婦檜」の名を持つ大きな御神木がある。中世には同社が所在する[[郡内地方]]の領主である[[小山田氏]]からの庇護を受けた。 [[ファイル:Kitagutihongu fujisengenjinjya 北口本宮富士浅間神社本殿.png|サムネイル|262x262ピクセル|北口本宮富士浅間神社本殿　一間社入母屋造り軒唐破風付き]] 富士登山道の吉田口の起点にあたり、[[江戸時代]]中期以降には富士講が流行し、上吉田ではこれを早くから受け入れたことから登山道の中心地となった。周辺には[[御師]]の[[宿坊]]が百件近く立ち並んだこともある。昭和初期には神社北の裏手から登山バス[[浅間神社 - 馬返線]]が運行していた。 江戸時代中期以降「諏訪大明神」よりも「浅間大菩薩」「富士浅間明神」の名のほうが大きくなり、[[明治]]時代には「冨士山北口本宮冨士嶽神社」と改称。その後「浅間神社」とも名乗るようになり、[[1946年]]（[[昭和]]21年）に現在の「北口本宮冨士浅間神社」と改称した。 のちに[[扶桑教]]を起こす[[宍野半]]は当社の社司と[[富士山本宮浅間大社]]宮司を兼務していた。そのため隣接地には扶桑教元祠があり、現在も扶桑教ではここから吉田口登山道を登って頂上に至り、富士宮口登山道を下って浅間大社まで参拝している。 == 諏訪明神と浅間明神 == === 北口本宮冨士浅間神社 摂社 「諏訪神社」 === ==== 祭神 ==== * 建御名方神（たけみなかたのかみ） * 八坂刀売神（やさかとめのかみ） ==== 例祭 ==== * 鎮火祭 （[[吉田の火祭]]）- 8月26日、27日 ==== 由緒 ==== 諏訪神社は元々は当地域の氏神であったが[[明治維新]]の際に北口本宮の[[摂社]]となった。 [[勧請]]年代は不詳であるが、下記のことから、当初鎮座していたのは浅間神社ではなく、諏訪神社であったと考えられている。 『[[甲斐国志]]』巻之七十一神社部第十七上「諏方明神」の記述からも古社であることが窺える。古来より社中に「諏訪の森」が位置し、[[諏訪神社]]の鎮座地に浅間神社を[[勧請]]したと伝わる。 {{Quotation|往古ヨリ此社中ヲ諏方ノ森ト称スルハ、'''浅間明神勧請セザル以前ヨリ諏方明神鎮座アル故'''ナリト云、古文書二諏方ノ森浅間明神トアル是ナリ}} [[天文 (元号)|天文]]17年（[[1548年]]）5月26日、[[小山田信有]]{{要曖昧さ回避|date=2016年1月}}は吉田の諏訪禰宜に富士山神事の際に新宮を建てる場合は披露するように命じている。[[永禄]]4年（[[1561年]]）3月2日、[[武田信玄]]は吉田の諏訪の森の木を伐ることを禁止している。『甲斐国志』によると、同年に武田信玄が富士権現を造営したとある。これらの事柄から、永禄4年（[[1561年]]）の信玄による富士権現造営が現在の北口本宮冨士浅間神社の元になるものであるとし、それ以前は諏訪社のみが鎮座していたとする笹本正治は、小山田信有が富士山に関する神事を諏訪禰宜に命じていることから当時諏訪社のみが鎮座していたとし、また永禄期の信玄の施策は、信玄の富士信仰の一端であるとしている。。 吉田の火祭として知られる鎮火祭は諏訪神社の例祭である。 === 小室浅間明神との関係 === 浅間明神の勧請元は、『甲斐国志』の下記の記載によれば、吉田口二合目の小室浅間神社（現在の[[冨士御室浅間神社]]）である。 {{Quotation|是古社殿ナキ以前富士浅間遥拝ノ地ニ築ク後神祠ヲ創造シ'''小室浅間明神'''ヲ勧請スト云}} 本来「下浅間」とは当社を指しているという{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.pref.yamanashi.jp/fujisan/rebirth/documents/fujisanmichi-omote.pdf|title=富士参詣富士山道表|accessdate=２０１９．０２|publisher=山梨県富士山世界文化遺産保存活用推進協議会}}。 [[延宝]]8年（[[1680年]]）の登拝路や信仰施設を描いた『八葉九尊図』で現北口本宮は「下浅間」と記されている{{Cite journal|author=串田優子 伊藤裕久|year=2006|title=北口本宮冨士浅間神社境内空間の変遷過程|journal=日本建築学会計画系論文集|volume=第604号|page=159-166}}。また、『甲斐国志』の記載から、文化11年（1814年）の時点では、「上浅間」が冨士御室浅間神社、「下浅間」が北口本宮冨士浅間神社、それとは別に冨士山下宮小室浅間神社が「下ノ宮浅間」と呼ばれていた。{{Quotation|小室ヲ'''上浅間'''ト云此祠ヲ'''下浅間'''ト稱スルハ本小室ト同社ノ謂ナリトソ、又下吉田ニ浅間アリ是ヲハ'''下ノ宮浅間'''ト稱ス}} しかしながら、現在では北口本宮が「上浅間」と呼ばれ、[[冨士山下宮小室浅間神社]]が「下浅間」と呼ばれることが多い。 富士吉田地域に於いて、北口本宮が浅間神社としては新しく、富士講御師に依る対外的な信仰を集めていたのに対して、冨士山下宮小室浅間神社は富士北麓地域の[[産土神]]・[[鎮守神]]で、農耕信仰を中心とした地元民の生活に根差した信仰があった。 だが、明治に入り、北口本宮には冨士山下宮小室浅間神社から氏子地域である上吉田を譲られ、氏神としても信仰されるようになり、それぞれ上吉田の浅間神社「上浅間」、下吉田の浅間神社「下浅間」と呼ばれるようになった。 == 文化財 == === 国指定重要文化財 === * 北口本宮冨士浅間神社東宮本殿（建造物） - [[1907年]]（明治40年）8月28日指定。 * 拝殿の東の裏側に立っており、「富士次郎杉」と呼ばれ市民に親しまれている。 * 北口本宮冨士浅間神社の[[ヒノキ]] - 拝殿前向かって右側に立ち、2本のヒノキが根元で1本になった合着木で、地上約3ｍから2幹に分岐し、約12ｍで再び接合しているところから「富士夫婦桧」と呼ばれている。 == エピソード == * 権禰宜によると、隣接地においてかつて富士山自動車という企業が事業を営んでいたが、同社が廃業した際に土地を中国人が購入しそうになった。そこで[[富士急行]]が当該土地を買収し、参拝者が増えた際の臨時駐車場として無料で開放している。それ以外の用途は現状無く、同権禰宜によれば「富士急行が志で神社の為に購入した」ものであるという{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~)。 {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|ja|富士山}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration."{{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fuji cult|ja|富士講}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|shukubō|ja|宿坊}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|12=draft}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県|12=draft}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|12=draft}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|ja|富士山|12=draft}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration."{{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{citation needed|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine}} ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=draft}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=draft}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=draft}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=draft}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=draft}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=draft}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fuji cult|ja|富士講|12=draft}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|shukubō|ja|宿坊|12=draft}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=draft}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=draft}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} |shintai= |shakaku=Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|近代Rank制度#諸社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|qq=}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiyoshida|qq=}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamanashi Prefecture|qq=}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|ja|富士山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Fuji|qq=}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fuji cult|ja|富士講|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuji cult|qq=}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|shukubō|ja|宿坊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shukubō|qq=}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamanashi Prefecture|qq=}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiyoshida|qq=}} Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|qq=}} {{ill|Mt. Fuji Station|qq=}}. ==Related Articles== * {{ill|Yoshida Fire festival|ja|吉田の火祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Fire festival|qq=}} * {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|ja|富士講|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiko (religion)|qq=}} * {{ill|Gekkō-ji Temple|ja|月江寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gekkō-ji Temple|qq=}} * {{ill|Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|ja|冨士御室浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|qq=}} * {{ill|Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|ja|冨士山下宮小室浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Kōshū Dōguyū|ja|郡内大工仲間|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōshū Dōguyū|qq=}} * {{ill|Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|ja|三國第一山新倉富士浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|qq=}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Further Reading== * Masaharu Sasamoto, "Takeda Shingen and Fuji Faith," in The Warring States Daimyō Takeda Clan, Meicho Publishing, 1991 ==External Links== {{osm box|n|2783245651}} *[https://www.sengenjinja.jp Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine] {{Commonscat|Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration}} {{Historic Sites Mount Fuji}} {{Tōkai Nature Trail (Shizuoka/Yamanashi Prefecture section)}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{Asama Faith}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{translated page|ja|北口本宮冨士浅間神社|version=104554522|comment=Imported full ja history}} }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]] [[Category:U Completion categories]] [[Category: [[sn:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]] [[ja:北口本宮冨士浅間神社]] [[en:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]]

{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|qq=}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiyoshida|qq=}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamanashi Prefecture|qq=}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|ja|富士山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Fuji|qq=}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fuji cult|ja|富士講|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuji cult|qq=}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|shukubō|ja|宿坊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shukubō|qq=}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|ja|富士山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Fuji|qq=}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fuji cult|ja|富士講|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuji cult|qq=}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|shukubō|ja|宿坊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shukubō|qq=}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|ja|山梨県|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamanashi Prefecture|qq=}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|ja|富士吉田市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiyoshida|qq=}} Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|qq=}} {{ill|Mt. Fuji Station|ja|富士山駅|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mt. {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|天孫彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} |shintai= |shakaku=Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|近代Rank制度#諸社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}
[[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|qq=}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Kamiyoshida, [[:en:Fujiyoshida|Fujiyoshida]], [[:en:Yamanashi Prefecture|Yamanashi Prefecture]]. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of [[:en:Mount Fuji|Mount Fuji]], and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fuji cult]], financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 [[:en:Shukubo|shukubō]] (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * [[:en:Yamanashi Prefecture|Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[:en:Fujiyoshida|Fujiyoshida]] Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|qq=}} [[:en:Mt. Fuji Station|Mt. Fuji Station]]. ==Related Articles== * {{ill|Yoshida Fire Festival|lt=Yoshida Fire Festival|lt=Yoshida Fire festival|ja|吉田の火祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Fire festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fujiko (religion)]] * {{ill|Gekkō-ji Temple|ja|月江寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gekkō-ji Temple|qq=}} * {{ill|Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|ja|冨士御室浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|qq=}} * {{ill|Omuro Sengen Shrine (Yamanashi)|lt=Omuro Sengen Shrine (Yamanashi)|lt=Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|ja|冨士山下宮小室浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Kōshū Dōguyū|ja|郡内大工仲間|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōshū Dōguyū|qq=}} * {{ill|Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|ja|三國第一山新倉富士浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|qq=}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Further Reading== * Masaharu Sasamoto, "Takeda Shingen and Fuji Faith," in The Warring States Daimyō Takeda Clan, Meicho Publishing, 1991 ==External Links== {{osm box|n|2783245651}} *[https://www.sengenjinja.jp Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine] {{Commonscat|Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration}} {{Historic Sites Mount Fuji}} {{Tōkai Nature Trail (Shizuoka/Yamanashi Prefecture section)}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{Asama Faith}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{translated page|ja|北口本宮冨士浅間神社|version=104554522|comment=Imported full ja history}} }} {{draft categories| [[Category:U Completion categories]] [[Category: [[sn:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]] [[ja:北口本宮冨士浅間神社]] [[en:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]]

Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of [[:en:Mount Fuji|Mount Fuji]], and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fuji cult]], financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 [[:en:Shukubo|shukubō]] (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of [[:en:Mount Fuji|Mount Fuji]], and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fuji cult]], financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 [[:en:Shukubo|shukubō]] (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fuji cult]], financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|天孫彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}}

[[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|qq=}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Kamiyoshida, [[:en:Fujiyoshida|Fujiyoshida]], [[:en:Yamanashi Prefecture|Yamanashi Prefecture]]. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of [[:en:Mount Fuji|Mount Fuji]], and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|qq=}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|qq=}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|qq=}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|qq=}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|qq=}}, the leader of the [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fuji cult]], financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 [[:en:Shukubo|shukubō]] (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|qq=}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * [[:en:Yamanashi Prefecture|Yamanashi Prefecture]] [[:en:Fujiyoshida|Fujiyoshida]] Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|qq=}} [[:en:Mt. Fuji Station|Mt. Fuji Station]]. ==Related Articles== * {{ill|Yoshida Fire Festival|lt=Yoshida Fire Festival|lt=Yoshida Fire festival|ja|吉田の火祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Fire festival|qq=}} * [[:en:Fujiko (religion)|Fujiko (religion)]] * {{ill|Gekkō-ji Temple|ja|月江寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gekkō-ji Temple|qq=}} * {{ill|Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|ja|冨士御室浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|qq=}} * {{ill|Omuro Sengen Shrine (Yamanashi)|lt=Omuro Sengen Shrine (Yamanashi)|lt=Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|ja|冨士山下宮小室浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujisan Shita-miya Komuro Asama Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Kōshū Dōguyū|ja|郡内大工仲間|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōshū Dōguyū|qq=}} * {{ill|Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|ja|三國第一山新倉富士浅間神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakura Fuji Asama Shrine|qq=}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Further Reading== * Masaharu Sasamoto, "Takeda Shingen and Fuji Faith," in The Warring States Daimyō Takeda Clan, Meicho Publishing, 1991 ==External Links== {{osm box|n|2783245651}} *[https://www.sengenjinja.jp Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine] {{Commonscat|Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen Shrine}} {{Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration}} {{Historic Sites Mount Fuji}} {{Tōkai Nature Trail (Shizuoka/Yamanashi Prefecture section)}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{Asama Faith}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{translated page|ja|北口本宮冨士浅間神社|version=104554522|comment=Imported full ja history}} }} {{draft categories| [[Category:U Completion categories]] [[Category: [[sn:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]] [[ja:北口本宮冨士浅間神社]] [[en:Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:安土桃山時代の建築]] [[Category:室町時代の建築]] [[Category:富士吉田市の建築物]] [[Category:富士吉田市の歴史]] [[Category:Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration]] [[Category:山梨県にある国指定の史跡]]
