In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. Ōtorii (photographed August 26, 2019) {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=250|coord={{coord|35|28|14.8|N|138|47|32.6|E}}}} |location={{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida}} Kamiyoshida 5558 |latitude_deg=35|latitude_min=28|latitude_sec=14.8|N/S=N |longitude_deg=138|longitude_min=47|longitude_sec=32.6|E/W=E |map_country_code=JP |map=Japan Yamanashi |deity={{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}
{{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|天孫彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} |shintai= |shakaku=Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|近代Rank制度#諸社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|WD=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|WD=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|WD=Q11455614|lt=shukubō}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida}} Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富士山麓電気鉄道富士急行線|1=Fujikyuko Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5507433}} [[:en:Mt. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|WD=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult|1=Fujiko (religion)}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|WD=Q11455614|lt=shukubō|1=Shukubo}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). {{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|WD=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji|1=Mount Fuji}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|WD=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult|1=Fujiko (religion)}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|WD=Q11455614|lt=shukubō|1=Shukubo}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|WD=Q11455614|lt=shukubō|1=Shukubo}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. {{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|WD=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji|1=Mount Fuji}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|WD=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult|1=Fujiko (religion)}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. Ōtorii (photographed August 26, 2019) {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=250|coord={{coord|35|28|14.8|N|138|47|32.6|E}}}} |location={{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}} Kamiyoshida 5558 |latitude_deg=35|latitude_min=28|latitude_sec=14.8|N/S=N |longitude_deg=138|longitude_min=47|longitude_sec=32.6|E/W=E |map_country_code=JP |map=Japan Yamanashi |deity={{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}

{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} |shintai= |shakaku=Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|近代Rank制度#諸社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|WD=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji|1=Mount Fuji}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|WD=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult|1=Fujiko (religion)}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|WD=Q11455614|lt=shukubō|1=Shukubo}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Designated March 28, 1923 File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a1.jpg|First Torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a2.jpg|Approach (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826a4.jpg|Approach viewed from the large torii (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826b4.jpg|Chōzuya (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c2.jpg|Taro Sugi (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826c1.jpg|Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d4.jpg|Hinomiko-sha and Ike Nibasha (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d5.jpg|Suwa Shrine Haiden (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d7.jpg|Suwa Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) File:Kitaguchi Hongu Fuji Sengen jinja 20190826d8.jpg|Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Departure festival (photographed August 26, 2019) ===National Historic Sites=== * Included in the National Historic Site "Mount Fuji" ===Prefectural Natural Monuments=== * Fuji Sengen Shrine's Great Cedar - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|WD=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|WD=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}} Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富士山麓電気鉄道富士急行線|1=Fujikyuko Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5507433}} [[:en:Mt. Fuji Station|Mt. {{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|qid=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} |established=Traditionally 40th year of Emperor Keikō (during {{ill|Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja|日本武尊の東征|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru's eastward expedition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) |honden= |other_names= |fudasyo_etc= |main_festival=Hatsusumij-sai (May 5) |shinji= }} '''Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine''' (北口本宮冨士浅間神社, Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Kamiyoshida, {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|qid=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|qid=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代Rank制度|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was that of a Prefectural Shrine, and it is now designated as a Beppyo Shrine under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|qid=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji|1=Mount Fuji}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|qid=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult|1=Fujiko (religion)}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|qid=Q11455614|lt=shukubō|1=Shukubo}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - It serves as the starting point for the Yoshida Trail of {{ill|Mount Fuji|en|Mount Fuji|qid=Q39231|lt=Mount Fuji|1=Mount Fuji}}, and is part of the "Mount Fuji" component of the World Cultural Heritage Site "Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration." ==deity== * {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} (Konohanasakuya-hime no Mikoto) * Heavenly grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|ja|彦火瓊瓊杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Hikohono Ninigi no Mikoto) - Husband deity * {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamatsumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオヤマツミ}} (Ōyamatsumi) - Father deity ==Major festivals== * New Year festival - February 17 * Hatsusumij-sai (festival) - May 5 * Chinka-sai (Yoshida Fire festival) - August 26, 27 * Niinamesai - November 23 ==History== In the 40th year of Emperor Keikō, it is said that during his eastward expedition, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} passed through the area, where he enshrined a deity and built a small shrine at the command to ascend Mount Fuji from the north side. In the 7th year of Enryaku (788), the Governor of Kai Province, {{ill|Ki no Toyonawa|ja|紀豊庭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Toyonawa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, constructed the current shrine and enshrined the great deity of Asama, along with the spirit of Yamato Takeru at Ōtsukaoka. The shrine has undergone various reconstructions and renovations over the centuries, with the current main hall built in Genwa 1 (1615) by the Lord of {{ill|Tanimura Castle|ja|谷村城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanimura Castle|1=Tanimura Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11632966}}, Tosa-no-Kami Torii Seiji. The shrine buildings were renovated again in Jōkyō 5 (1688). In Kyōhō 18 (1733), {{ill|Muraoka Mitsukiyo|ja|村上光清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muraoka Mitsukiyo|1=Murakami Kōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11522718}}, the leader of the {{ill|Fujiko (religion)|en|Fujiko (religion)|qid=Q11456201|lt=Fuji cult|1=Fujiko (religion)}}, financed and built the Heiden, Haiden, Kaguraden, Chōzuya, and Zuishinmon. The shrine is located at the starting point of the Yoshida Trail of Mount Fuji, and during the Edo period, it became the center of the Fuji cult. At its peak, the area had nearly 100 {{ill|Shukubo|en|Shukubo|qid=Q11455614|lt=shukubō|1=Shukubo}} (lodging houses for pilgrims). In the early Shōwa period, a bus route was operated from the back of the shrine to the Mount Fuji climbing route. During the Edo period, the name "Asama Ōbōsatsu" became more prominent than "Suwa Daimyōjin." In the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Fujisan Kitaguchi Hongū Fujidake Shrine," and later simply "Sengen Shrine." In 1946, it was renamed to its current name, "Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine." The shrine's connection to {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} was established when {{ill|Shinano no Okami|ja|信濃大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano no Okami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Suwa Myōjin) was merged into Kitaguchi Hongū as a subsidiary shrine. ==Cultural Properties== ===Important Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine East Hall (Structure) - Designated August 28, 1907 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine West Hall (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall (附: 1 board) (Structure) - Designated March 31, 1953 * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine 8 buildings (Structure) - Designated November 28, 2017 ** Haiden and Heiden ** Ebisu-sha and Tōbei ** Kaguraden ** Chōzuya (附: 1 board) ** Zuishinmon (附: 1 board) ** Fukuchi Hachiman-sha (附: 2 boards) ** Suwa Shrine Haiden ** Office (附: 1 board) ** (附 designated) Lantern 1 piece * Tachi Sword with inscription "Bishu Osafune Kageie Bun'an 2nd year February" (附: Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (Craftwork) - Located to the left of the Haiden, called "Fuji Taro Sugi," estimated to be around 1,000 years old. ===Prefectural Intangible Folk Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine Grand Kagura ===Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine main hall Ema (5 pieces) (附: Silk colored Fuji Mountain Northern View) (Paintings) ** Colored wooden panel painting of camellia and bamboo shoots (2 pieces) - Donated in Genwa 4 (1618) by Tosa-no-Kami Torii. ** Colored wooden panel painting of horse decoration and pine monkey (2 pieces) - Painted by Kano Tsuneshige, donated in Genroku 1 (1688) by Tajima-no-Kami Akimoto. ** Colored gold ground painting of divine horse (1 piece) - Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors. According to the Deputy Priest, Fuji Kyūkō purchased the land "for the sake of the shrine out of goodwill" without any other intended use{{Citation|title=【前田日明】日本武尊の聖域を参拝！！不思議な現象も？【久保サラ夫妻】|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GaEeHx62UX4|accessdate=2021-06-15|language=ja-JP}}（7:40~). ==location== * {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|qid=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture|1=Yamanashi Prefecture}} {{ill|Fujiyoshida|en|Fujiyoshida|qid=Q647508|lt=Fujiyoshida|1=Fujiyoshida}} Kamiyoshida 5558 ==Access== * Train: Approximately 25 minutes on foot from {{ill|Fujikyu Line|ja|富士急行線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujikyu Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富士山麓電気鉄道富士急行線|1=Fujikyuko Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5507433}} [[:en:Mt. Painted by Kano Dokuen Nashin, donated in Genroku 11 (1698) by Noto-no-Kami Toda Tadashige. * Wooden seated statues of guardian deities (附: pedestals) (Sculpture) - Two statues with blue and red garments, made in Eisho 17 (1520) by Minbu Hokkyo, a disciple of Hitachiobo from Gojō Ōmiya, Kyoto. * Fuji Diary (Ancient document) - A travel diary written by Kamo Tadayoshi, a scholar of kokugaku residing in Edo, when he visited the area in Kansei 2 (1790). ===Municipal Natural Monuments=== * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Cedar - Located behind the Haiden to the east, called "Fuji Jiro Sugi" and cherished by locals. * Kitaguchi Hongū Fuji Sengen Shrine's Hinoki - Two hinoki trees fused at the base, called "Fuji Meoto Hinoki," meaning "Fuji Husband and Wife Cypress." ==Episode== * According to the Deputy Priest, there was a business named Fujisan Jidōsha (Mount Fuji Automobile) operating on adjacent land. When the company went out of business, the land was nearly purchased by Chinese investors. Fuji Kyūkō stepped in and bought the land, offering it as a free parking lot for shrine visitors.
